text:
maria: hitting a weird SSL handshake error when onboarding a Dedicated customer behind their corporate proxy + custom CA. sample app works locally but fails in their k8s cluster. stack: python-sdk async client, aiohttp, requests proxy envs set. error: SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED (depth=0)

aj: can you paste the minimal code you use to create the client? also are you setting REDWOOD_BASE_URL or passing base_url to the client?

maria: minimal snippet:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
async def main():
    c = AsyncClient(base_url="https://dedicated.example.com", api_key="...", proxy="http://10.0.0.1:3128", ca_bundle="/etc/ssl/redwood-ca.pem")
    await c.generate("hi")
```

it fails during TLS handshake. note: the cluster has an explicit sidecar proxy and custom CA is in a mounted file. i also tried setting HTTPS_PROXY env var and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE. same failure.

samir: two quick possibilities: 1) aiohttp's connector isn't picking up cert from requests env vars, you need to pass an ssl.SSLContext with load_verify_locations(cafile=...) 2) if the proxy is doing TLS interception, you must ensure the proxy trusts the upstream certs or that the client trusts the proxy's CA.

maria: thx. how would i do the ssl.SSLContext approach?

samir: something like:
```python
import ssl
from redwood import AsyncClient
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/redwood-ca.pem')
# if you want to force no system trust: ssl_ctx.check_hostname = True
client = AsyncClient(base_url='https://dedicated.example.com', api_key='...', connector_args={'ssl': ssl_ctx, 'trust_env': False})
```

note: current SDK exposes connector_args for aiohttp but it's not well-documented; we should probably add a truststore_path param in the constructor.

olivia: fwiw i've seen typing issues with connector_args typing in the py client. mypy complains because AsyncClient constructor signature is narrow. adding a TypedDict for connector_args or a named param would help DX.

aj: also watch out for auth retry: we had a bug where token refresh retries went through the proxy with no ssl context and got 401, causing a tight retry loop. please check logs for repeated "refresh token failed" messages.

maria: yes! saw repeated 401s in logs right after the cert error. after applying the ssl ctx -> the cert error went away but then requests started failing during token refresh with 502 from proxy.

samir: proxy 502 often means CONNECT to upstream failed. two angles: 1) proxy is intercepting CONNECT and requires SNI/correct host header 2) our client might be sending chunked transfer or http2 that proxy doesn't like. can you try forcing HTTP/1.1 on connector?

maria: quick test results: forcing ssl ctx + forcing http1 fixed handshake and generation works, but mypy flags on code that constructs AsyncClient with connector_args. also the sample Dockerfile we give to customers doesn't show the system-level cert install steps for Debian/Alpine which adds friction.

olivia: proposed small DX items:
- add connector_ssl arg or truststore_path param to AsyncClient constructor (typed)
- ensure sdk respects REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / SSL_CERT_FILE for both sync/async paths
- document dockerfile and k8s initContainer to update OS truststore (example for debian and alpine)
- fix retry logic so refresh tokens reuse the same ssl context when doing proxy requests

aj: i can file a GH issue with labels: devex, py-sdk, security, customer-onboard. mari? can you paste a short repro and the failing logs (scrubbed)?

maria: pasted a redacted log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T14:02:10Z maria kube-proxy: CONNECT dedicated.example.com:443 failed: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:997)
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z maria auth: token refresh failed 401 via proxy
```

aj: ok thanks. creating issue and linking repro + suggested patch for connector_args typing.

devx-bot: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/4721 — "py-sdk: add truststore param and ensure ssl context used on refresh retries (customer onboarding)" (assigned aj) :rocket:

maria: one more onboarding note — customers expect a one-liner env var to work (REDWOOD_BASE_URL + HTTPS_PROXY + SSL_CERT_FILE). if SDK could fallback to reading SSL_CERT_FILE automatically for async we could avoid most friction.

samir: agreed — i can PR the code for aiohttp connector to read SSL_CERT_FILE when connector_args['ssl'] is not provided. we'll also add a small sample k8s job in /examples/onprem that mounts the CA, runs update-ca-certificates and sets SSL_CERT_FILE.

olivia: and i'll follow-up with a mypy-friendly typing PR; propose adding types: connector_args: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] and a top-level param truststore_path: Optional[str].

maria: thanks team — workaround is in place for now (ssl ctx + http1), will keep the customer updated. opened a short internal onboarding doc in docs/onboarding/dedicated-proxy.md and linked the issue. :+1:
